title: Lumi-Lai
prompt:
Original uplifting Afro-pop dance song for a beautiful fantasy-island rhythm game, sunny festival energy, joyful and melodic, polished contemporary pop production. Exactly 112 BPM in steady 4/4. Crisp prominent kick, dry snare/claps, bright shakers and syncopated congas, warm bouncing bass, clean plucked guitar and playful marimba. A clear stable landing pulse underneath the syncopation. A completely new melody, harmony and arrangement.

The signature vocal language is LUMI-LAI: a soft, clear, airy HUMAN female lead singing invented words with real pop phrasing, expressive breath, a warm mid-register and a beautiful memorable melody. The vocals must feel like a full lyrical pop song, with flowing verse sentences and a soaring chorus, although every word is imaginary. Charming and suitable for children and teens, without sounding like a nursery rhyme. Occasional quiet human backing harmonies support the lead.

Sing only combinations of this sound vocabulary: "lumi-lai", "lumi-la", "liya-lo", "eiya-lai", and occasional brief "tiri-ti" or "tiri-ta" accents. Pronunciation: loo-mee-lie, loo-mee-lah, lee-yah-loh, ay-yah-lie, tee-ree-tee. Hyphens indicate pronunciation, not separate beat attacks. Flow naturally across the beat, vary syllable and note lengths; sustain the open vowel in "laaai" for 1-2 beats at selected phrase ends. Use rapid "tiri-ti" on occasional eighth-note turnarounds, leaving room around those accents. Keep a strong recognisable Lumi-lai hook while varying phrasing between sections. The vocal sounds are invented sung words rather than animal sounds. No meows, barks, other animal imitations, sound-effect voices, pew-pew, ordinary-language words, spoken instructions or section labels. No shrill chipmunk voice or robotic chopped-vocal delivery.

Suggested original vocal phrases, interpreted as natural sung melodic lines:
"Lumi-la, liya-lo, lumi-laaai"
"Liya-lo, eiya-lai, lumi-la"
"Tiri-ti, lumi-la, eiya-laaai"
"Lumi-lai, lumi-lai, liya-lo"
"Ei-ya-lai, lumi-la, lumi-laaai"
"Tiri-ti, tiri-ta, lumi-lai"
These are a phonetic palette, not a monotonously looped chant. Develop a fresh musical melody and coherent question-and-answer phrases from them.

Make a COMPLETE short song approximately 90 seconds long with a proper harmonic ending, targeting 42 bars at 112 BPM: 2-bar bright instrumental intro (about 4 seconds), 8-bar flowing melodic verse, 8-bar catchy expansive chorus, 4-bar lighter rhythmic interlude with a few tiri-ti responses, 8-bar varied second verse, 8-bar energetic final chorus with gentle harmonies, 4-bar resolving outro ending in a crisp coordinated final hit. Preserve momentum and stable tempo throughout. Strong vocal and percussion accents suitable for jumping between tiles, a few held vocal notes for slides, contrasting phrasing and a clear final musical resolution. Keep vocals forward and articulate, restrained reverb, percussion transients clean. No long intro, tempo change, cinematic swell or fade-out. Finish the whole musical piece around 90 seconds. Entirely original composition and performance; quote no existing melody, lyrics or recording.
